title: Titanium Spoke Nipple
function: Hexagonal spoke nipple for rim interface
alloyReason: Grade 5 Ti-6Al-4V (Grade 5, UNS R56400) was selected for this wheel hardware application because its 900+ MPa tensile enables thin-wall lightweighting under cyclic loading. The alpha-beta microstructure provides 45% higher specific strength than 4140 steel, critical for weight-sensitive designs. Its 6.7 W/mK thermal conductivity simplifies thermal management. This rationale is driven by hexagonal spoke nipple for rim interface and service environment demands.
process: CNC turning Swiss-type for wheel hardware geometry

surfaceTreatment: Bead blasting 120 grit Al2O3 for matte finish Ra 1.6-3.2um followed by passive oxide stabilization in DI water — tailored for hexagonal spoke nipple application
commonFailures: Bearing race brinelling from over-torque - avoided by torque-limiting press-fit tool with ±2% accuracy — critical for hexagonal spoke nipple performance

faq.q: What specific material properties make Titanium Spoke Nipple suitable for Hexagonal spoke nipple for rim interface?
faq.a: Titanium Spoke Nipple uses Grade 5 Ti-6Al-4V because its yield strength, fatigue endurance, and corrosion resistance directly address wheel hardware operational demands. The alloy's specific strength enables mass reduction without section compromise, while the TiO2 passivation ensures long-term environmental resistance.

faq.q: What are the critical dimensional tolerances for Titanium Spoke Nipple?
faq.a: Standard machining tolerance for Titanium Spoke Nipple is +/-0.05mm (ISO 2768-m). Functional mating surfaces are held to +/-0.025mm with Ra 0.8um finish, verified specifically for hexagonal spoke nipple requirements. Threaded features conform to ISO 965-2 Class 6g, verified with calibrated Go/No-Go ring gauges on 100% of production.

faq.q: Does Titanium Spoke Nipple require any post-machining surface treatment?
faq.a: Yes. hexagonal spoke nipple components require Bead blasting 120 grit Al2O3 for matte finish Ra 1.6-3.2um followed by passive oxide stabilization in DI water — tailored for hexagonal spoke nipple application. This restores the natural TiO2 passive layer removed during machining and provides the required surface properties for the specific service environment. Key parameters include surface finish Ra 0.8um and passive layer thickness verification per applicable standards.
